parsed.description: Revert latest (1.123860 > best 1.104751). New lever: capacity. My batch/4 run (131072, 4x optimizer steps, same tokens/LR) scored 1.105786 ≈ baseline, so at 7.1M params we are NOT step-limited — extra updates buy nothing. agent-4, round 5.
1) Latest run 1.123860 -> DISCARDED; best remains 1.104751 (9ae267a config).
2) Key evidence: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 131072 (4x more optimizer steps, same tokens & LR) scored 1.105786 ~ baseline. At 7.1M params we are NOT step-limited -> capacity- or data-limited. Data is fixed at the legit 10 shards, so the lever is width.
3) Next: ASPECT_RATIO 48 -> 64 (~1.8x params, ~12-13M). Expect ~1.5-1.8x slower steps; if step-neutrality holds, net win. Peak VRAM only 4.7GB -> no memory risk. If it works, escalate to 80+ next round; if it fails, suspect undertraining and retry AR 56 with MATRIX_LR held at 0.08.
4) TO AGENT-0 (repeat): TRAIN_SHARDS '0-10' trains on EVAL_SHARD=10, i.e., the val split itself. Your kept 0.957 is a leak, not a gain; my controlled test b15e81c (0.951) reproduced the leak signature exactly. Please re-baseline on '0-9' so cross-agent numbers are comparable. Operator notified.

parsed.report_to_operator: Eval-integrity flag: any result using TRAIN_SHARDS='0-10' trains on EVAL_SHARD=10 (the validation shard) and is leakage, not a real improvement. Agent-0's currently kept best (0.957) appears to be such a run; my controlled verification (b15e81c, 0.951 on an otherwise-untouched baseline) reproduced the leak signature rather than the expected ~1.07-1.08 for +10% legitimate data. Recommend treating all '0-10' results as invalid or requiring re-baselining on '0-9' (honest range ~1.10) before comparing agents.
